_comment: OVERLAY on seed-profile.json. Seam I8 — the reshaped fixture.
seed-profile.json is provenance: extracted by lib/extract-seed-profile.py from a real
production dump, and it is NOT edited here. Changing a measured distribution in place
would turn a measurement into an assertion, and nothing downstream would know.
This file states only the values that are deliberately overridden, and why each one is.
WHAT I8 FIXES. The 443k reference dataset was built by duplicating a smaller dump 20x.
That compressed the time axis to ~33 days and froze cardinality at 1x, so every scan
reported examined ~= 401,240 at BOTH -30 and -90 days. No date-range conclusion taken on
it is falsifiable, and no index conclusion either: a report that ignores the range filter
entirely returns the same number as one that honours it.

_why_resource: Measured value is 1,326 distinct resources. A4's cliff is MySQL switching an internal
temporary table from MEMORY to disk, which a GROUP BY resource crosses somewhere above
~2,048 distinct values on the default max_heap_table_size. At 1,326 the fixture sits
BELOW the cliff, so no query in the suite has ever gone to disk for a temp table and
the whole class of defect is unreachable — including the one A4 names.
4096 is chosen to sit clearly past it rather than on it: a fixture that lands ON a
threshold measures the threshold's jitter, not the code. The synthesised tail comes from
the seeder's existing filler, so the head of the distribution keeps its measured skew and
only the long tail is manufactured — which is what selectivity depends on.
_why_referer: Raised in proportion (1,602 -> 4,096) so the referer report's grouping crosses the same
cliff. Leaving it at the measured value would make 'top referrers' the one report that
still cannot exercise the defect, for no reason a reader could infer.

_time_axis: Not an overlay value — a CALLER obligation, stated here because this is where someone
looks. seed.php takes `days` as its second argument, and I8 requires >= 120 so that a
30-day window and a 90-day window select genuinely different row sets.
tests/docker/seed-bench.sh passes 180 and then VERIFIES the property rather than trusting
it: it fails if rows(30d) is not strictly less than rows(90d), and if rows(90d) is not
strictly less than the total. A fixture that cannot tell the ranges apart is the exact
defect I8 exists to remove, and it must not be possible to build one and call it done.
